title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test as implemented in the archived analysis yields two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts under the executor's exact-binomial convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; the measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier converted a single concrete baseline failure to a pass (pair id pair-000237; summary provided in Results). All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are rapidly being applied to NetOps tasks including intent-to-configuration translation, change planning, and repair automation. Operational safety in these systems commonly depends on surrounding engineering (deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, rollback), and a recurring architectural pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): the LLM proposes a configuration, a deterministic verifier checks formalized properties, and automated or human-in-the-loop repair resolves violations. Despite conceptual consensus that such guardrails improve safety, controlled measurements that isolate the verifier's marginal contribution while holding the model's proposal fixed are scarce. We therefore preregistered and executed a paired experiment to answer a focused operational question: given identical initial proposals (shared_initial_candidate semantics), how much does adding a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared with the LLM alone?
sections.related_work: Deterministic verifiers and formal analyses (header-space analysis, Batfish-style verifiers, route-model checks) provide machine-checkable properties like reachability, isolation, and update-atomicity and are well established in NetOps verification literature [Beckett et al., 2017]. Concurrently, recent NetOps/AIOps and agentic frameworks integrate LLMs for intent parsing and configuration generation while advocating guardrails (e.g., INTA, Confucius, and other agentic NetOps proposals) [Wei et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair patterns are proposed across structured-generation domains to reduce unsafe outputs [PoeTone; INTA]. Separate work documents systemic LLM failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, tool integration errors) and recommends verification or human oversight as mitigations [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. What is less prevalent is a preregistered ablation that quantifies the marginal verifier effect while keeping the LLM’s initial output identical for both arms; our study delivers that artifact-backed measurement.
sections.methodology:
We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026 and froze hypotheses, inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic task seeds, estimands, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule prior to execution. Primary confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations.

Task corpus and strata. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was generated (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and stratified into VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters. The realized per-cluster sample sizes matched the preregistered allocation: VLAN-change = 167, ACL-change = 167, static-route-change = 166 (recorded in the archived task manifest). The generator constrained tasks to feature constructs supported by the verifier (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}); exclusion and replacement rules were deterministic and preregistered; no confirmatory exclusions occurred.

Experimental semantics and controls. To isolate verifier+repair marginal effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false): for each task a single shared LLM proposal was produced and recorded; that candidate served as the baseline proposal and was also the subject of verification in the guarded arm. The guarded arm invoked at most one automated repair call only if the verifier reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate. This design prevents conflation with verifier-guided regeneration and isolates the effect of verification plus at most one repair applied to the same initial proposal.

Models, adapter, and verifier. The requested LLM was gpt-5-mini called via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses); model parameters (max_output_tokens = 2000, single-attempt generation) are archived in execution/model_configuration.json. The deterministic verifier used for gating and scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; its validator-spec and the mapping of violation codes to severity are archived. The guarded arm permitted at most one automated repair iteration per preregistered contract.

Analysis plan. The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. The archived analysis executor implements this by forming n = n10 + n01 (discordant pairs) and performing an exact binomial test on the observed n10 under H0: p = 0.5 (executor’s discordant-ordering convention yields the archived two-sided p reported). Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) were computed for the absolute difference by resampling pairs with replacement (pairing preserved). Missingness and retry policies were applied as preregistered; execution accounting and logs were archived.
sections.results:
Execution and aggregated outcomes. The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts: baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) is: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The archived exact McNemar two-sided test implementation yields p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts under the executor's exact-binomial convention on discordant pairs.

Discordant episode (archived deterministic identifier and sanitized summary). The single discordant episode is recorded under pair id pair-000237 in the archived execution results. Validator diagnostics for pair-000237 show that the baseline shared candidate violated a preregistered high-severity workflow constraint: a "must_be_down_for_field: vlan" violation (the candidate issued a VLAN change while the affected interface was reported admin=up), classified as high/medium severity per the archived validator-spec. The automated repair-stage call inserted an explicit interface shutdown command before the VLAN change and restored admin up afterward (repair pattern: insert 'interface <X> admin down' preceding the VLAN assignment and 'interface <X> admin up' after). After applying this single automated repair the verifier reported no remaining high/medium-severity violations and the guarded arm passed. The full validator_trace and repair provider-call trace for pair-000237 are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and linked artifacts for deterministic re-inspection.

Power and sensitivity. The preregistration assumed baseline error prevalence p_b≈0.30 and planned N=500 to achieve adequate power for a 10-percentage-point absolute reduction target. Observed baseline failure prevalence was 1/500, producing a ceiling effect that reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements. Consequently secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative due to near-zero counts. Diagnostics in analysis artifacts indicate no exclusions, no contamination flags, and zero failed episodes under the execution contract.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained experimental regime (single requested LLM gpt-5-mini, shared_initial_candidate semantics, deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set, and at most one automated repair iteration) the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals for the verifier-modeled properties and the marginal measured pass-rate improvement of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This is a conditional and operationally specific result: when baseline proposal quality is very high on the verifier-scoped properties, a modest verifier+repair budget may yield negligible measurable gains on a composite pass/fail metric, although the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures (as in pair-000237).

Design-choice implications. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals; this is relevant when deployment semantics require repairing a single human-reviewed proposal rather than regenerating. The experiment does not evaluate verifier-guided regeneration, multiple repair iterations, or cost-weighted tradeoffs; those operational alternatives require separate preregistered studies.

Threats to validity. Internal validity benefits from preregistration, deterministic seeds, and automated replacement rules; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity is limited by verifier coverage: success==no high/medium-severity violations is defined relative to the verifier’s modeled property set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}); properties outside that scope are not measured. External validity is limited by a single requested model, synthetic tasks, and constrained CLI-feature coverage; results do not generalize to multi-model, cross-vendor CLIs, or dynamic protocol states.

Statistical nuance. The archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the executor's exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs computation and the empirical discordant counts (n = 1). Small-sample exact p-values can be non-intuitive; here p = 1.00 indicates the observed pattern (one guarded-only success) is not improbable under the null when only a single discordant pair exists. The paired-bootstrap CI provides complementary uncertainty quantification for the absolute difference. Together they show that while a point improvement exists (0.002), inference is constrained by a ceiling effect and very small discordant counts.
sections.conclusion: We performed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the executor's convention). This conditional measurement documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for verifier-modeled properties and verifier coverage is limited, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a modest verifier+repair budget can be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric, though a verifier may still correct rare concrete failures (here pair-000237). Practitioners should measure baseline error prevalence on representative workloads, align verifier coverage with operator-critical properties, and select generation/repair semantics that match deployment priorities. All preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of every claim made here.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (pair-000237) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
